rows.scope: Deaths whose mode is drowning among cases handled by Maine's Office of Chief Medical Examiner, calendar 2021. All manners: the OCME says these deaths may be accidents, suicides or homicides, and its definitions allow a drowning to be ruled undetermined. No split by water, place or activity is printed; boating drownings are not separated. The report does not say whether it counts by place of death or residence.

A reviewer should confirm it by eye.

tried: CDC, Drowning data (https://www.cdc.gov/drowning/data-research/index.html, last reviewed 27 Jan 2026): the state map of 2018-2021 rates is an image; no Maine value appears in the page text, and no data-table link was found.
CDC WONDER and WISQARS answer only an interactive session; not attempted.
Maine OCME 2023 Annual Report (https://digitalmaine.com/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1031&context=ag_docs): the automated reader got a client error on 23 Nov 2026.
Maine OCME 2019 Annual Report (https://core.ac.uk/download/483942301.pdf), p. 8: prints 2017 as 27, 2018 as 33, 2019 as 29; older than the five-year window, recorded here only as a cross-check.
Looked for a Maine split by water (sea, lake, river, pool): none in the OCME reports; the Maine Warden Service search-and-rescue reports count searches, not drowning deaths, and were not used.
notes: Maine's medical examiner prints a yearly drowning count across all manners, so the five rows (2021-2025) come from two of its annual reports, which agree on the one year they share (2022: 31). These are OCME case counts by mode of death, not CDC's unintentional W65-W74/V90/V92 definition, so they are expected to differ from any CDC WONDER count for Maine. A 2021 Portland Press Herald article attributed to the medical examiner's office gave 34 (2018), 32 (2019) and 43 (2020); the OCME reports print 33, 29 and 43. Press, so not used for any row; it suggests counts can be revised after a report. The only activity split found is recreational boating (Coast Guard, 2025 only). The 2025 firearm figure (358, against 192 in 2024) is outside this task, but the report's own sentence says firearm deaths increased, so the row does not look misaligned. No figures were summed.
